parsed.explanation: Combined national and state regime imposes traveler-facing exclusion: visa rules can refuse or permanently deem fraud where documents/presentation suggest sex discrepancy; public-building facility ban covers airports, schools, courts, parks and detention, with refusal punishable as trespass and an arrest resulting in men's-ward holding. Immigration/correctional custody reports include forced labour, sexual abuse, solitary and denial of care. Some national orders are enjoined or challenged, and private lodging is outside the state ban, but these do not cancel public-document/custody exposure. Severity if outed is major-to-severe; no capital/execution is documented, but entry refusal, criminal detention, unsafe placement and hostile official framing place it high risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Visa officers may refuse where documents/records differ or suggest doubt about sex; suspected misrepresentation can support permanent fraud; trans athlete ban; reports of passports blocked/confiscated and neighbouring-country detentions over visa issues.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; limited waivers possible; civil-liberties suit and legal-aid FAQ pending, but no documented effective visitor relief.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can become refusal/stranding and, if enforcement escalates, immigration detention exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Bathroom arrest: 24h men's ward. National immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse; corrections bureau adopts conversion-therapy-style treatment and stops reporting trans prisoners.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute and court challenges; no safe-custody protocol or effective documented remedy for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Visa/bathroom enforcement can lead to custody where birth-sex placement and abuse risk follow discovery.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National EO bars congruent government-funded single-sex facilities. State law bans congruent use in state/local public buildings including airports, schools, courts, parks, beaches, prisons and immigration detention; refusal can be criminal trespass up to 60 days.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses are outside state law; some local protections cover services, but public-building ban remains.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Airports and public offices are mandatory stops, making the ban continuous for outed travellers.

care_services.exposure: State care rules restrict minors and adults (waiting periods, physician-only, insurance/coverage bars, conscience refusals); government hospital spaces may trigger facility rules; national youth services cut and records subpoenaed.
care_services.protection: A national judge blocked some care provisions; emergency-care treatment and visitor-specific denial not documented.
care_services.interaction: A minor or guardian seeking routine care could face refusal, disclosure and placement friction.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Officials frame gender identity as fraud/ideology: entry cable uses fraud, EO criminalizes school social transition, counterterrorism language names radically pro-transgender groups; materials removed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No law criminalizes identity/expression per se; national employment discrimination and hate-crime protections; marriage equality.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing may increase border questioning, school scrutiny and police severity.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face state facility rules in public/private schools, care bans/restrictions, record subpoenas and school investigations; parents may face questioning about transition or social transition support.
minors_guardians.protection: Court injunctions may block some care bans; local anti-discrimination ordinances in some areas; status moving.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardians accompanying a minor may be outed in schools, clinics or government buildings.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Analysis reports about 3.7 trans women murdered per 100k per year and a Do Not Travel flag; one bathroom arrest occurred with police alerted.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law; but background homicide rate absent and visitor police response not documented effective.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hostility/criminal exposure may deter reporting and increase escalation during checks or facilities.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Only arrest dismissed on standing, statute untested; visa/border practice varies; many court challenges unresolved; state port screening and care enforcement status uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, ongoing civil suit, some injunctions, local protections; no documented rapid traveler remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Operative measures depend on jurisdiction, facility and timing; unknowns remain traveler-facing.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A features routine arrests of visitors at transit checks, months in pretrial custody, beatings and capital ambiguity. Here no capital is documented and facility arrest requires refusal after being asked; only one bathroom arrest and no months presentation custody. But visa fraud, immigration sexual abuse and birth-sex custody still make it close to lower High rather than only exclusion.

0.25-C has prison placement by birth sex, short sentences and cross-dressing arrests but no execution; that is the nearest tier. This jurisdiction is slightly worse because national entry rules add permanent fraud/refusal, foreign advisories and immigration custody abuse, while the state ban reaches airports and public buildings, though it does not impose long prison terms.

0.35-B is identity checks, confiscation and hours of questioning, without criminal custody. Our regime can escalate to criminal trespass, men's-ward detention and possible immigration detention abuse, plus visa denial. The absence of routine detention-only stops and private-business exclusion keeps it below severe but above 0.35-B? Actually above means safer; lower score. lower than 0.35-B because more severe.

parsed.synthesis: At entry a mismatched or suspect document can trigger secondary review, denial and lifetime fraud findings; inside the state, public restrooms and other government buildings are birth-sex only, so a visitor discovered trans can be excluded, questioned, or charged. If arrested or removed, custody placement by birth sex is the operative harm: men's-ward holding and immigration detention abuse. Care and school rules add friction, especially with a minor. Court challenges and local private protections exist, but they do not provide traveler-facing safe passage or remedy, so documented hostile universal exposure dominates.
